tools.name: actions_chat_approve_confirmation
tools.description: Approve a low/medium-risk pending confirmation from chat after the user replies with the exact approval phrase returned by actions_request_confirmation or actions_get_confirmation_preview. High-risk, tainted, paid, expired, stale, or account-mismatched confirmations are denied and must use the browser approval URL.

confirmation_id.description: The pac_* confirmation id to approve.

approval_phrase.description: The exact approval_phrase the user replied with, e.g. 'Approve Zevari action pac_... code 123456'.

tools.name: actions_chat_reject_confirmation
tools.description: Reject a pending confirmation from chat after the user replies with the exact reject phrase returned by actions_get_confirmation_preview.

confirmation_id.description: The pac_* confirmation id to reject.

rejection_phrase.description: The exact reject_phrase the user replied with, e.g. 'Reject Zevari action pac_...'.

tools.name: actions_chat_update_confirmation
tools.description: Revise a pending single-action confirmation before approval. Provide a complete replacement_payload using the same executing tool schema. The server re-normalizes the payload, recomputes hashes/risk/approval channels, increments revision, rotates any chat approval phrase, and invalidates prior approval phrases. Bulk confirmations and campaign_v2_enroll confirmations are not editable through this tool; change one lead's message in a waiting campaign_v2_enroll batch with campaigns_v2_update_lead_message.

confirmation_id.description: The pac_* confirmation id to revise.

replacement_payload.description: The COMPLETE replacement payload for the original action_type. Start from actions_get_confirmation_preview.preview_payload, apply the user's requested edits, and include every required field.

tools.name: actions_dry_run
tools.description: Preview exactly what an action would do WITHOUT doing it and without staging anything. Returns the canonical payload and its hash, the resolved lead context, a current safety evaluation, and any gates that would block or warn. Creates no confirmation, no receipt, no audit intent and no queue row, and performs NO LinkedIn or email WRITE — nothing is sent, invited, posted or changed. Note it may perform read-only provider lookups while resolving a recipient (the same ones staging performs), so this is not a zero-network preview. Use it to check a payload, show the user what would be sent, or find out whether an action would be blocked before committing to an approval. IMPORTANT: the safety numbers are an evaluation, NOT a reservation (evaluation.authoritative is always false) — capacity can be consumed by another action between this preview and the send, so never describe the result as guaranteed. It reports would_block_on_safety (null = could not determine) and gates_not_evaluated — a false there means no safety-budget denial, NOT that the action would succeed, since execution applies further gates this preview cannot run. To actually perform the action, stage it with actions_request_confirmation afterwards.

action_type.description: The action family to preview. Same allowlist as actions_request_confirmation.

payload.description: The COMPLETE action payload you would stage, in the same shape actions_request_confirmation expects. It is validated and canonicalized by the same code, so a payload rejected here would be rejected there for the same reason.

tools.name: actions_get_confirmation_preview
tools.description: Fetch the canonical server-staged preview for a pending confirmation, including risk_class, operating context, approval channels, browser approval URL, and any chat approval phrase. Show this preview to the user before asking them to approve or reject.

confirmation_id.description: The pac_* confirmation id returned by actions_request_confirmation or actions_request_bulk_confirmation.

tools.name: actions_get_receipt
tools.description: Fetch one durable action receipt by its rcpt_* id: lifecycle status (queued/executing/succeeded/failed/deferred/rejected/cancelled/outcome_unknown), every linked identifier (confirmation, request, audit intent/outcome, LinkedIn object ids), the safety snapshot, and the hydrated lead_context. Linked sends add action_id, action_status (queued/started/sent/failed/cancelled/outcome_unknown), not_before, next_try_after for queued actions, and a customer-safe reason. Queued means next try after that time, not guaranteed delivery then. Existing receipt status values are unchanged. Receipts are returned in every LinkedIn write response as action.receipt_id. An outcome_unknown status means the LinkedIn response was lost — the action may have landed; do NOT retry it automatically. Planned campaign steps carry written_by (who composed the words: your_ai, zevari, or together) and sent_by: zevari. Zevari delivers every campaign message; delivery is not authorship.

receipt_id.description: The rcpt_* receipt id from a write response's action.receipt_id or a recent_activity item.

tools.name: actions_list_for_lead
tools.description: Page through the action history for one saved lead (newest first, default 50 per page, max 100). Items carry receipt ids/status where receipt linkage exists (receipt era), plus campaign ids, request/confirmation/audit ids, LinkedIn object ids, safety decision, and normalized error codes. Linked sends add live action_id, action_status (queued/started/sent/failed/cancelled/outcome_unknown), not_before, next_try_after for queued actions, and a customer-safe reason. Queued means next try after that time, not guaranteed delivery then. Existing history status values are unchanged. Never automatically retry outcome_unknown. The first call freezes an as_of snapshot and optional from/to bounds; pass the returned next_cursor to continue the SAME frozen result set (do not pass from/to again). Continues seamlessly from lead_context.recent_activity.next_cursor. Planned campaign steps carry written_by (who composed the words: your_ai, zevari, or together) and sent_by: zevari. Zevari delivers every campaign message; delivery is not authorship.

lead_id.description: The saved lead's lead_id (from lead_context.lead.lead_id or leads_* tools).

tools.name: actions_request_bulk_confirmation
tools.description: Stage multiple destructive actions under one approval URL. PREFER THIS over actions_request_confirmation when you have ≥2 outbound write actions to stage in this turn — the user reviews and approves all items in one click instead of opening N separate links. Allowlisted child action_types: linkedin_send_message, linkedin_send_inmail, linkedin_send_connection_request, linkedin_comment_on_post, linkedin_react_to_post, linkedin_create_post. Server returns one approval_url plus per-item ids; each child is later executed by the corresponding tool with both confirmation_id and bulk_item_id.

items.description: Ordered list of child actions to bundle under one approval URL. Server assigns item_ids; AI-supplied ids are ignored.

action_type.description: Child action_type. Must be in the v1 bulk allowlist.

payload.description: Per-item payload using the underlying tool's input schema. linkedin_send_connection_request accepts identifier, provider aliases, saved lead IDs, public identifiers, and profile URLs; Zevari canonicalizes each child before approval. Comment/reaction postId values are resolved to the post's social_id before approval.

tools.name: actions_request_confirmation
tools.description: Stage an approval-gated destructive or sensitive action for user approval. Call before single outbound LinkedIn/email writes, campaign activation, and the allowlisted actions in action_type. Personalized campaign enrollment is not staged here: call campaigns.addTargets with personalized_steps instead (it stages campaign_enroll_personalized_targets internally and returns the retry when approval is needed). Do NOT use for entity-persistence tools (targets_save, profile_update, content_save, etc.) — call those directly. Approval: eligible low/medium-risk actions return chat_approval.approval_phrase (show it, then call actions_chat_approve_confirmation) plus approval_url as browser fallback. Bulk: for 2+ outbound LinkedIn actions in one turn use actions_request_bulk_confirmation (one URL covers all). Errors: campaign_activate stages only for draft or paused campaigns; active, processing, terminal, or archived campaigns return CAMPAIGN_INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION before any confirmation is created or Autopilot is evaluated (terminal recovery: create a new campaign).

action_type.description: The exact allowlisted action family this confirmation gates. Valid values are LinkedIn/email sends/InMails/posts/comments/reactions, campaign_activate, campaign_update_target_set, campaign_update_step_config, bulk_delete, bulk_export, and agents_enrich_email_batch. For campaign activation, use 'campaign_activate' with payload={campaign_id: <id>}. Personalized enrollment must use campaigns.addTargets, which stages its receipt-bound confirmation internally. Entity saves such as targets_save are not valid action_types and do not need confirmation.

payload.description: The COMPLETE action payload. LinkedIn writes are validated at stage time; connection requests accept saved lead/provider/public/profile URL aliases and are stored as canonical provider-ID payloads, while linkedin_comment_on_post/linkedin_react_to_post postId values are resolved to the post's social_id before approval. After approval, execution uses this stored approved payload as the source of truth.

config.description: New step config. Canonical outbound fields per action_type: connect→message (optional, ≤300 chars) or messages{slug:text}; message→body (required) or messages{slug:text}; comment→comment_text (required) or messages{slug:text}. For new LinkedIn campaign maps, use exact linkedin_provider_id (ACoAAA...) keys only; for email maps, use exact lead_email keys only. Omit from_address unless the user explicitly provided one; Zevari resolves the verified sender. POST DESTINATIONS (canonical): set config.post_refs = { "<target_key>": { "id": "<numeric_activity_id>" } } for like_post / react_to_post / comment, or { "*": { "id": "..." } } for a global post. For connect/message contextual references, use config.context_post_refs with the same shape. To allow most-recent dynamic resolution, set config.post_resolution = "dynamic". For threaded replies, also set config.comment_id. Submitting config.post_id / post_url / context_post_id / context_post_url as object maps is rejected with invalid_post_destination_shape — use post_refs instead. Use config.instruction for internal notes. config.note is REJECTED.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_add_leads
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Add leads to a v2 campaign — one identity field each (URL, slug, provider id, gl_ lead id, or email); no status precondition. Omit campaign_id to run a sequence for one or a few people outside any campaign: each lead must then carry its own sequence, it runs from the active LinkedIn sender, and it shows under Activity → Sequences; call it a "sequence", not a campaign. LinkedIn steps need each lead's LinkedIn profile ID (starts ACo or ADo) saved; leads from Sales Navigator usually have only a Sales Navigator ID (starts ACw), so run linkedin_get_profile with identifier and lead_id for them first. Returns the partial-success envelope {added, duplicates, unresolved, suppressed, blocked, warnings, approval}. Manual approval returns approval.confirmation_id + approval.approval_url (always include the URL for the user). Collision holds appear in warnings as pending_confirmation with a STAGED coexist confirmation (coexist_confirmation_id + approval_url); once the USER approves it, re-call with coexist_confirmation_ids (cumulative across multiple conflicts).

identity.description: LinkedIn URL, vanity slug, provider id, gl_ lead id, or email.

action_type.description: Step action. Executable: 'message', 'connect', 'email_send', 'view_profile', 'like_post', 'comment_on_post', 'inmail', 'react_post_comment'. Sequence copy can use {{first_name}}, {{last_name}}, {{full_name}} and {{company_name}}, filled per lead at enroll, with a fallback for an empty value: {{first_name|there}}. Any other {{…}} is rejected, and a lead with no value and no fallback is held back as missing_variable_value. Copy is sent exactly as written, with the variables filled in. Zevari drafts a LinkedIn message body only when its step sets config.generation_mode "llm".

tools.name: campaigns_v2_create
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Create a v2 campaign with a template sequence. Campaigns are SEQUENCE-LOCKED BY DEFAULT: every lead runs exactly this sequence (topology frozen; message copy and delays stay editable) — pass sequence_locked=false for a campaign whose leads may carry bespoke sequences. Steps after the first need delay_hours >= 3 (override via settings.min_step_delay_hours), except the step right after a branch condition. Branch on connection acceptance or a usable email with config.routing (see the sequence step config); the structure is fixed at create, so build every branch in this call. Optional settings are sparse policy overrides. Optional goal/cta_resource_url/icp/notes/voice_user_id: omitted goal/ICP/CTA copy from the workspace Business Profile at create; voice defaults to the creator.

sequence.description: Template sequence (TEMPLATE ONLY — copied per lead at enroll).

tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Read one v2 campaign plus settings.raw/workspace/effective, intent (goal/ICP/CTA/notes/voice_user_id), send_window, and campaign.written_by. Zevari delivers every campaign message; written_by says who composed it (your_ai, zevari, or together). A send attributed to Zevari does not mean Zevari wrote the text.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_list
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. List v2 campaigns for the active workspace + LinkedIn account (id, name, status, lead counts, written_by). Archived campaigns are hidden unless include_archived=true. Zevari delivers every campaign message; written_by says who composed it (your_ai, zevari, or together). A send attributed to Zevari does not mean Zevari wrote the text.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_override_send_window
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Temporarily allow THIS campaign's outbound outside working hours (UT/ops hold bypass). Sets send_window_override_until and wakes sequences the runner marked as working-hours-held (does not pull forward intentional delays). Does NOT change user working hours (prefer this over settings_update_working_hours when progress reports a send hold). Pass clear=true to end early; otherwise the override expires after minutes (default 60, max 240).

tools.name: campaigns_v2_pause
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Pause a v2 campaign (reversible): sends halt immediately; scheduled steps stay queued and resume where they left off via campaigns_v2_resume. Nothing is skipped or stopped.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_pause_lead
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Pause ONE lead in a v2 campaign (reversible): the runner skips this lead while the rest of the campaign continues. Resume continues from the lead's current step, never from step 1. Terminal leads (completed/replied/stopped) cannot be paused.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_pending
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Read pending_review/scheduled v2 steps and open enrollment approvals for a campaign. pending_requests include confirmation_id and approval_url for manual enroll approvals.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_progress
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Per-lead, per-sequence progress: each sequence's cursor (stable step id), step totals, next_action_at, and lead profile fields read from the saved lead. Always includes send_window (working hours / currently_open / next_open_at). When outbound is frozen outside working hours with scheduled steps waiting, send_window.hold explains the pause and how to override via campaigns_v2_override_send_window. When the window is open but next_action_at is still in the future, wait for that pickup time — do not tell the user the worker is late or that sends "should have fired". Sent steps with words carry written_by and sent_by. Zevari delivers every campaign message; written_by says who composed it (your_ai, zevari, or together). A send attributed to Zevari does not mean Zevari wrote the text.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_remove_lead
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Remove one lead from a v2 campaign: skips unsent steps, stops the lead's sequences, marks the lead stopped, releases its outreach claim. History is preserved; re-adding later creates a fresh attempt (attempt_no + 1). An in-flight send cannot be recalled.

confirm_remove.description: Must be true — removal stops all future outreach to this lead in this campaign.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_resume
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Resume a paused v2 campaign: steps fire on their original schedule; any steps currently due send in the next working-hours tick (due_now_steps in the response).

tools.name: campaigns_v2_resume_lead
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Resume a paused lead in a v2 campaign: continues from the lead's current step; due steps fire in the next working-hours tick. Only 'paused' leads resume — re-add terminal leads via campaigns_v2_add_leads.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_schedule
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Consume an APPROVED campaign_v2_enroll confirmation and schedule the enrolled first steps (manual-approval completion; autopilot schedules inline at enroll).

tools.name: campaigns_v2_update_intent
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Replace/patch campaign intent fields (goal, cta_resource_url, icp, notes, voice_user_id). Provided keys replace; omitted keys keep prior values. Not for policy settings.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_update_lead_message
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Replace the outbound text of one step, guarded by the lead's version (optimistic lock). Before enrollment review it changes a draft step in place. While the lead's batch waits for approval it changes a draft or pending_review step and updates the waiting approval in the same call: show the user the returned approval phrase or link, because the old phrase stops working. After the lead was approved it changes any step no send has reached yet, through a new approval of the new wording (applied at once on Autopilot): show the user the returned link or phrase; until they approve, the lead keeps getting the current message. Sent copy never changes.

step_id.description: Step id (clst_…), from campaigns_v2_pending or campaigns_v2_progress.

message.description: The new outbound text for this step.

tools.name: campaigns_v2_update_settings
tools.description: Campaign V2. Executable steps: connect, message, email_send, view_profile, like_post, comment_on_post, inmail, react_post_comment. MCP tools never send directly; Zevari sends due steps after enroll + approval and send safety checks. scheduled is not sent. Merge-patch sparse policy settings on a v2 campaign (working hours / daily_new_leads / reply_handling / post_campaign_actions / timezone). Does not full-replace: omitted keys keep prior campaign overrides; keys never set still inherit workspace. Not for goal/ICP/notes/voice — use campaigns_v2_update_intent. lead_collision_policy is org-wide and rejected.

settings.description: Sparse patch object. Allowed keys: timezone, working_hours_only, working_hours_enabled, working_hours, min_step_delay_hours, daily_new_leads, reply_handling, post_campaign_actions. daily_new_leads = whole number 1-500: how many NEW leads start per day in this campaign. Everyone you add is still enrolled and approved at once; their first steps are spread over days, in the order added, inside working hours. Leads waiting for their day are counted as waiting_to_start_count (not active). Changing it reschedules leads that have not started; removing a waiting lead moves the rest up; null (update only) clears it and everyone starts as normal. Omit it for no limit. working_hours = {enabled, days:{mon:[{start:"HH:MM",end:"HH:MM"}],…,sun:[]}}; omit it to use the account working hours. reply_handling keys (booleans): stop_all_campaign_steps_on_reply, stop_linkedin_followups_on_reply, stop_email_followups_on_reply, alert_on_reply. post_campaign_actions keys: withdraw_unanswered_invites (auto|notify_only|off), withdraw_after_days (7-90), notify_before_withdrawal (boolean). Unanswered connection requests are withdrawn automatically by default: auto, 10 days after the invite was sent, with a heads-up email the day before. Unknown keys are rejected.

The search appears on the AI team → Prospecting page. For a one-off interactive search use linkedin_search_profiles instead.

On an EXHAUSTED search a plain call returns the exhausted status and does not rescan; pass scan_from_beginning=true to scan it again from the first page.

tools.description: Update a scheduled Sales Navigator saved search: rename, change cadence or per-run cap, pause/resume (enabled), move the destination list, or replace the search definition (URL/filters). Definition or list changes atomically RESET the scrape cursor and exhaustion latch and re-arm the schedule. To rescan an exhausted search without changing it, use linkedin_saved_search_run_now with scan_from_beginning=true.

filters.description: Structured Sales Navigator filters. Resolved to concrete LinkedIn parameter IDs at save time, so scheduled runs need no further input.

tools.name: linkedin_view_profile
tools.description: Trigger a LinkedIn profile view notification — used in warming sequences to get on a prospect's radar before connecting.

identifier.description: LinkedIn provider ID — triggers 'Someone viewed your profile'

tools.name: lists_delete
tools.description: Stage deletion of a lead list. This only creates a browser-only Zevari approval link; the list is not deleted until an owner/admin approves in the Zevari UI within 24 hours. Chat approval is not supported. By default leads remain in the workspace.

tools.name: lists_remove_member
tools.description: Stage removal of a lead from a list. This only creates a browser-only Zevari approval link; the membership is not removed until an owner/admin approves in the Zevari UI within 24 hours. Chat approval is not supported. The lead remains in the workspace.

lead_id.description: Lead ID to remove from the list

tools.name: media_assets_attach
tools.description: Attach a file the user already uploaded in Settings > Media to a draft post, by its library id (ma_…). This is the normal way to add an image or PDF to a post: the user uploads in Settings > Media, clicks Copy ID, and gives you the id. Only valid while the content is in 'draft' state — for a scheduled post call content_cancel first, attach, then content_schedule again. If the user has a local file but no id yet, tell them to upload it at https://zevari.ai/dashboard/settings?section=media (or directly on https://zevari.ai/dashboard/content/{contentId}).

content_id.description: Draft content row to attach to

media_asset_id.description: Library asset id (ma_…) from Settings > Media 'Copy ID'

tools.name: media_assets_attach_from_url
tools.description: Attach an image (JPG/PNG/GIF, max 8MB) or PDF (max 100MB) **already hosted at a public HTTPS URL** to a draft post. Only for files the user explicitly provides a public URL for. For a file uploaded in Settings > Media use media_assets_attach with its ma_ id instead; for a local file or an image attached in the chat, direct the user to https://zevari.ai/dashboard/content/{contentId} where they can upload directly. Only valid while content is in 'draft' state.

content_id.description: Draft content row to attach to

tools.name: media_assets_delete
tools.description: Delete a media asset and remove it from storage. Fails if the asset is still attached to any content row.

tools.name: media_assets_list
tools.description: List media attached to a content row, in render order.

content_id.description: Content row whose attachments to list

tools.name: notifications_get
tools.description: Get the notification routing config (Signal Routing) for a LinkedIn account: { account, org, can_manage, paused, paused_at, recipients[] (each with nested per-event routes + last_test), events[] (registry, excluding the test sentinel), warnings[] ({event_type, reason: 'no_recipient'|'only_unverified'}) }. Recipients are the resolved account's recipients UNIONed with org_default. Exact funded account access is enforced before any read; a no-account/org-default read is owner/admin only. Never returns signing secrets or verification tokens.

tools.name: notifications_test
tools.description: Send a TEST notification to a configured recipient (by id) in the active workspace/account to confirm its channel works. Any workspace member may use an exact funded LinkedIn account; org-default recipients require owner/admin access. Returns the delivery result and records it for the settings UI.

recipient_id.description: notification_recipients.id of the recipient to test.

tools.name: notifications_update
tools.description: Mutate notification routing (Signal Routing) config. One tool, five actions: add_recipient (email/webhook — webhook mints a signing secret returned ONCE), edit_recipient (label), remove_recipient (soft-delete), set_route (toggle/save an event→recipient route with cadence + min_intent_score), set_pause (pause/resume an account). Any workspace member may operate an exact funded account; org-default config is manager-only.

tools.name: objection_playbook_list
tools.description: List objection playbook entries by subtype, sender profile, status, and archive state.

tools.name: objection_playbook_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a versioned objection playbook entry. Approved versions are immutable.

tools.name: outbound_channels_get
tools.description: Preflight outbound readiness for the active Zevari workspace: active LinkedIn account, Zevari-managed verified email sender readiness, and optional target LinkedIn relationship status. MUST be called before creating LinkedIn message campaigns that omit connect; email campaigns may omit from_address because Zevari resolves the sender server-side.

tools.name: outreach_templates_create
tools.description: Create a new user-owned outreach template in the catalog.

slug.description: Lowercase slug (a-z, 0-9, hyphens). Must be unique within your account.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in the catalog

tools.name: outreach_templates_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a user-owned outreach template.

slug.description: Slug of your user-owned template to delete

tools.name: outreach_templates_fork
tools.description: Copy a system or existing template into a new user-owned template for customization.

source_slug.description: Slug of the template to fork (system or your own)

new_slug.description: Slug for the new fork (must be unique within your account)

tools.name: outreach_templates_get
tools.description: Fetch a single outreach template by slug, including its prompt components and optional version history.

tools.name: outreach_templates_list
tools.description: Browse the outreach template catalog by framework, scope, and status.

tools.name: outreach_templates_preview
tools.description: Fetch the prompt outline and sequence structure of a template for UI rendering or review.

slug.description: Slug of the template to preview

tools.name: outreach_templates_update
tools.description: Edit a user-owned outreach template; changes are versioned.

slug.description: Slug of the template to update

tools.name: profile_get
tools.description: Get the current user's business profile: persona, company, ICP criteria, default CTA, and preferred tone. Read this before generating any outreach.

tools.name: profile_update
tools.description: Update the user's business profile. Required before agent tools will produce accurate results.

tools.name: proof_assets_list
tools.description: List proof assets scoped to the workspace, optional sender profile, account, asset type, and approval status.

tools.name: proof_assets_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a proof asset with supported claims, objection subtypes, next-message jobs, and approval status.

tools.name: reply_context_get
tools.description: Read scoped conversation context for the MCP-facing AI before it makes a reply decision. Returns latest inbound message, recent thread, inbox triage, conversation state snapshot, last outbound touch, optional campaign attribution, campaign strategy context, proof/objection options, and a decision_input_hash. Read-only.

chat_id.description: LinkedIn chat id for the conversation.

latest_inbound_message_id.description: The newest visible inbound inbox_messages.id the AI is deciding on.

tools.name: reply_decisions_get
tools.description: Fetch a visible reply decision by decision_id or the active latest decision for a chat_id, including draft revision history and conversation state snapshot.

tools.name: safety_get_status
tools.description: Get unified safety status for the active organization and LinkedIn account: current pause state, tier, LinkedIn weeklyUsage/dailyCap/burst caps, delays, and recent safety events. weeklyUsage covers LinkedIn actions only — it never includes send_email. Email is not in this table: own-domain mailboxes (Resend, Brevo) have per-mailbox caps, and Instantly or Smartlead mailboxes use those tools' own sending limits; do not invent an org email weekly quota from weeklyUsage.

tools.name: settings_get_working_hours
tools.description: Get the active user's default automation working hours and timezone.

tools.name: settings_update_working_hours
tools.description: Update the active user's standing automation working hours and timezone (workspace-wide schedule). Prefer campaigns_v2_override_send_window when campaigns_v2_progress reports a send hold and you only need a temporary bypass for one campaign — client Auto Mode often blocks this standing-config tool.

working_hours.description: Default automation schedule. Windows must be non-overlapping and same-day.

tools.name: signal_keywords_get
tools.description: Read the LinkedIn account's keyword slots: the 9-slot entitlement, how slots are allocated across workspaces, every keyword assignment with its rotation state, and current scanner execution status. Assignments are what the signal scanner actually scans; scanner on/off and thresholds live separately on the agent config.

tools.name: signal_keywords_initialize
tools.description: Turn on keyword scanning for this LinkedIn account: sets up its 9 keyword slots and the keyword-posts source (the same as Add source → Keyword posts on the Prospecting page). Requires an active paid sender sponsorship. Run before the first signal_keywords_replace; safe to run again, and an existing source keeps its on/off state.

tools.name: signal_keywords_replace
tools.description: Replace the account's keyword allocation: which workspaces get how many of the 9 slots and the full keyword set per workspace. Version-guarded compare-and-set — read with signal_keywords_get first and pass the versions back. Moving a keyword between workspaces means creating it in the destination and pausing the source.

expected_entitlement_version.description: Entitlement version from the latest signal_keywords_get read (compare-and-set guard)

allocations.description: Full desired allocation state; this replaces, it does not merge

workspace_grant_id.description: Workspace grant id from signal_keywords_get; each grant may appear once

allocated_slots.description: Slots given to this workspace (the account-wide total across workspaces is capped at 9)

assignments.description: Full desired keyword set for this workspace; active count must fit allocated_slots

tools.name: signals_list
tools.description: List signals with optional filtering by type, priority, or acted status.

tools.name: signals_mark_acted
tools.description: Mark a signal as acted upon so it no longer appears in the active signal queue.

signal_id.description: Signal ID to mark as acted on

tools.name: signals_save
tools.description: Persist detected buying signals (hiring, funding, pain point, etc.) linked to a lead and/or post.

tools.name: skills_activate
tools.description: Activate a skill for the current user with initial configuration.

tools.name: skills_get
tools.description: Get a skill's step-by-step instructions, config schema, and metadata by slug. Read these instructions before executing the skill.

tools.name: skills_list
tools.description: List available skills by category. Always call this before complex workflows to check if a skill exists.

tools.name: skills_update_config
tools.description: Update a user's skill configuration (e.g., change default settings).

tools.name: targets_archive
tools.description: Stage archive of a lead. This is destructive cleanup and only creates a browser-only Zevari approval link; nothing is archived until an owner/admin approves in the Zevari UI within 24 hours. Chat approval is not supported. Prefer archive for bad ICP matches or leads the user wants hidden from default views.

tools.name: targets_create_list
tools.description: Create a named list and optionally add leads to it.

tools.name: targets_delete
tools.description: Stage hard deletion of a lead. This is destructive cleanup and only creates a browser-only Zevari approval link; nothing is deleted until an owner/admin approves in the Zevari UI within 24 hours. Chat approval is not supported. Use only for records created by mistake, not ordinary disqualification.

tools.name: targets_get_pipeline
tools.description: Query leads by pipeline status with pagination.

tools.name: targets_save
tools.description: Persist one or more actionable LinkedIn profiles as trackable leads in global_leads. This is an entity persistence tool and does not require actions_request_confirmation; call it directly. Include linkedin_provider_id when available; linkedin_profile_url/linkedin_url/profileUrl/publicIdentifier are accepted identity aliases.

targets.description: Array of target profiles to save

tools.name: targets_save_research
tools.description: Store research output (ICP score, behavioral profile, company intel) against an existing lead record.

tools.name: targets_update_status
tools.description: Update a lead's pipeline status (discovered, contacted, qualified, converted, disqualified).

tools.name: voice_dna_save
tools.description: Save a user's writing style profile extracted from their own LinkedIn content.

style_system.description: Complete voice profile: syntax_patterns, vocabulary, tone, formatting, outreach_style

tools.name: voice_profiles_delete
tools.description: Remove a voice layer's copy so voice resolution falls through to the next layer. Idempotent: deleting an absent layer returns deleted=false, not an error.

scope.description: Voice layer: "user" (the caller's promoted canonical voice), "workspace", or "campaign".

tools.name: voice_profiles_get
tools.description: Read one voice layer (user/workspace/campaign): stored sections, effective values, revision, inherited-from lineage, and voice_source. Never 404s — a scope with no row returns the default surface.

scope.description: Voice layer: "user" (the caller's promoted canonical voice), "workspace", or "campaign".

tools.name: voice_profiles_init
tools.description: Create a voice layer by copying an existing source into it: source=effective (default) copies the ad-hoc voice resolution for the caller, source=user copies the caller's own user_voice_dna row for the active workspace (not the canonical scope='user' layer), source=workspace copies the workspace voice. Returns already_exists if the scope already has a row.

scope.description: Voice layer: "user" (the caller's promoted canonical voice), "workspace", or "campaign".

tools.name: voice_profiles_patch
tools.description: Edit a voice layer's sections with patch semantics: omitted sections are retained, typed empties clear. Every write requires expected_revision (CAS). Read voice_profiles_get first and re-read on content_dna_conflict.

scope.description: Voice layer: "user" (the caller's promoted canonical voice), "workspace", or "campaign".

expected_revision.description: Compare-and-swap token (integer) from voice_profiles_get; mismatch returns content_dna_conflict

tools.name: zevari_context_confirm
tools.description: Lock this chat to a Zevari organization and LinkedIn account after the user explicitly confirms it, either by resuming a context lock (context_lock_id) or by confirming a scope from zevari_context_get.available_contexts (organization_id and linkedin_account_id). Only this chat changes; other chats and scheduled tasks keep their own contexts. Do not call this until the user has confirmed the intended organization/account in natural language, unless the task instructions name the context lock or IDs to use.

user_confirmation.description: Short natural-language summary of the user's confirmation, e.g. 'User confirmed Manvi Workspace / Manvi LinkedIn for this chat.'

tools.name: zevari_context_get
tools.description: Start-of-chat Zevari MCP context check. Call this before any other Zevari tool in a fresh chat. It returns this chat's context lock (if any), the user's active context locks, the available organizations and LinkedIn accounts, and handover prompts for chats that should operate in a different scope.

tools.name: zevari_context_locks
tools.description: List the user's active Zevari context locks, or extend or revoke one. A context lock pins an organization and LinkedIn account until it expires, for every chat or scheduled task that resumes it. Extend and revoke need the user's explicit agreement.

action.description: list: the user's active context locks. extend: lengthen one lock. revoke: end one lock for every chat and task using it.

tools.name: zevari_org_users_list
tools.description: List active users/members in the current confirmed Zevari organization. Owner/admin callers also receive pending invitations. Use this when the user asks who is in the current org/workspace/team.

tools.name: zevari_reparent_account
tools.description: Operator-only account separation: re-own one user's MOVE-class data/knowledge (leads, lists, signals, research, content) from one org/LinkedIn-account scope to another via the owner-lane reparent step. Campaigns + provider/execution/audit are intentionally RETAINED with the separating operator (the beneficiary recreates outreach). Workflow: run with dry_run=true first to preview table_counts, stage an account_reparent confirmation, then re-call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_id to apply. The subscription org pointer moves atomically inside the function on a cross-org separation; reconcile Stripe afterward with zevari_transfer_billing_ownership. To roll back, re-run with from/to swapped under the same idempotency_key.

target_user_id.description: Zevari user_id of the account being separated/moved.

from_org_id.description: Source org_id that currently owns the target's data/knowledge.

to_org_id.description: Destination org_id that should own the target's data/knowledge after the move.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key for this reparent operation. Re-applying the same key is a no-op. To roll back, re-run with from/to scopes swapped under this same key.

tools.name: zevari_transfer_billing_ownership
tools.description: Operator-only account separation, billing reconcile step. The subscription/org pointer already moved atomically inside the reparent step, so this tool does NOT do a second cross-org write. It reads the reparent reconcile view for drift on the target and returns the exact Stripe instructions — metadata.org_id AND the identity carriers metadata.user_id/metadata.owner_user_id per expected_stripe_identity (stale identity carriers make every later subscription webhook fail billing_identity_mismatch) — to be applied only through the operator billing tool. reconciled=true when the reconcile view returns zero drift rows.

target_user_id.description: Zevari user_id whose billing/org pointer is being reconciled.

to_org_id.description: Destination org_id the subscription metadata should point at.

idempotency_key.description: REQUIRED: the same idempotency_key used for the zevari_reparent_account apply step. Used to confirm an applied reparent operation into to_org_id exists before reporting reconciliation, so the tool never returns a false reconciled=true when no operation ran.
